results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila [mushroom body](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00005801 "Open mushroom body in Virtual Fly Brain") are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the Virtual Fly Brain database. According to the Virtual Fly Brain database, the mushroom body is divided into these three parts: the calyx, which receives sensory interneuron afferents; the pedunculus, a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes; and the mushroom body lobe system, which consists of a vertical branch and a medial branch, with different structures at different life stages. VFB holds various records related to the mushroom body, including images, neurons with some part in the mushroom body, and parts of the mushroom body, with counts of [2](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of mushroom body") images, [602](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,NeuronsPartHere "Run in VFB: Neurons with some part in mushroom body") neurons with some part in the mushroom body, and [176](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00005801,PartsOf "Run in VFB: Parts of mushroom body") parts of the mushroom body. For further information, you can explore the available data in VFB, such as the images of neurons with some part in the mushroom body or the tracts/nerves innervating the mushroom body.

results.title: Neuron characterisation
results.question: What is known about the LPLC2 visual neuron type? Where is it, what does it connect to, and what is its function?
results.response:
The LPLC2 visual neuron type has specific characteristics and functions. Its cell body is located in the dorsal area of the lateral cell body rind. The LPLC2 neuron has a distinct dendritic arbor in each lobula plate layer, extending outwards from the main fiber in the direction of motion detection for the layer, which allows it to detect looming stimuli. In the lobula, it has its main dendritic arbors in layers 4 and 5B, with minor processes in layer 5A, and presynaptic sites in layer 4. The arbors of LPLC2 neurons span approximately 25 lobula optic columns, overlapping with other LPLC2 cells. 

LPLC2 neurons project to an optic glomerulus of the PVLP, anterior to LPLC1 and dorsal to LC4. The activity of LPLC2 neurons elicits a jump escape response. VFB holds data on approximately 80 of these cells per optic lobe, and they are cholinergic. 

VFB does not currently hold comprehensive data on all connections of the LPLC2 neuron type, but it is known to project to the PVLP. For more detailed information on the connectivity of LPLC2 neurons, further queries can be made to explore available connectome data.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior. According to VFB, it has a unique anatomy and connectivity, with one cell per hemisphere, and its large cell body is located posterior to the lower protocerebrum. The giant fiber neuron can be identified by its large descending axon, which is several times larger than any other axon in the cervical connective. It enters the cervical connective via the posterior cerebro-cervical fascicle and descends on the ipsilateral side, in the dorsal cervical fasciculus. In the brain, it has dendritic arborization in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center, where it receives substantial input from zone A and B Johnston organ neurons. It also arborizes in the posterior ventrolateral protocerebrum and gorget. The giant fiber neuron forms electrical synapses with downstream motor and premotor neurons at the inframedial bridge, where the two giant fiber neurons connect across the midline, and at the axonal lateral bend.

VFB records show that the giant fiber neuron is a primary neuron. Available driver lines include [P{R48A11-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R30C01-p65.AD} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0121835FBtp0118557 "Open P{R48A11-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R30C01-p65.AD} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain"), [P{R68A06-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0116198FBtp0118471 "Open P{R68A06-GAL4.DBD} ∩ P{R25C08-p65.AD} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain"), [P{GMR91H05-GAL4} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0064022 "Open P{GMR91H05-GAL4} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain"), [P{GMR79D08-GAL4} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0063022 "Open P{GMR79D08-GAL4} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain"), [P{GMR78G07-GAL4} expression pattern](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/VFBexp_FBtp0062972 "Open P{GMR78G07-GAL4} expression pattern in Virtual Fly Brain").

The connectivity of the giant fiber neuron can be described based on the available data. VFB holds [389](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records of downstream connectivity classes for the giant fiber neuron and [472](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") records of upstream connectivity classes. 

Relevant publications include Thomas and Wyman (1984), Koto et al. (1981), Namiki et al. (2018), Power (1948), Ito et al. (2014), Kamikouchi et al. (2009), Matsuo et al. (2016), Kim et al. (2020), King and Wyman (1980), Allen et al. (1998), Kennedy and Broadie (2018). 

VFB has annotated [23](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") images of the giant fiber neuron, [5](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,SplitsTargeting "Run in VFB: Splits targeting DNp01") splits targeting it, and [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") transgene expression patterns in this neuron.
